answers.children: Yes — Cavalier King Charles Spaniels are good with children because of their gentle nature, affectionate temperament and high tolerance for handling. Their small but sturdy build and sociable disposition let them curl up patiently on a toddler’s lap or endure ear-tugging without protest. The breed’s original purpose as a royal companion supports this calm adaptability around family members of all ages. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 9/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Cavalier King Charles Spaniels get along well with other pets thanks to their sociable and gentle temperament. They rarely show aggression toward dogs or cats and their history as pure companions rather than hunters means they lack strong prey drive. Their affectionate personality usually leads to harmonious multi-pet households.
answers.exercise: Cavalier King Charles Spaniels need two 20- to 30-minute walks daily plus short play sessions. Without this they gain weight quickly, which is especially risky given their low robustness. Light backyard romps chasing a ball or gentle indoor zooming suit their moderate energy and small silky-coated build.
answers.shedding: Yes — Cavalier King Charles Spaniels shed moderately with no strong seasonal pattern. Their medium-length silky coat with feathering on the ears and tail releases loose hair that clings to furniture and clothing. Regular brushing removes the dead hair before it spreads through the house.
answers.hypoallergenic: The Cavalier King Charles Spaniel has a medium silky coat that sheds moderately and spreads fine hairs across furniture and clothing. Its feathering on ears and tail traps dander that becomes airborne in a home. No dog is genuinely hypoallergenic, and a Cavalier is not one of the breeds usually put forward for allergy sufferers. (PawLabs shedding score: 5/10)
answers.training: Cavalier King Charles Spaniels are moderately easy to train because of their affectionate nature and desire to please. Their biddable temperament responds well to gentle guidance yet their original role as undemanding companions can make them sensitive to harsh methods and occasionally distracted by the wish for closeness.
answers.lifespan: Cavalier King Charles Spaniels live 12-15 years. Their health robustness is low and the breed is prone to serious heart conditions that can shorten life. The silky-coated toy build requires owners to monitor weight and activity levels carefully to support the longest possible lifespan within that range.
answers.size: Cavalier King Charles Spaniels reach 13-18 lb and stand 12-13 in at the shoulder. Their small yet well-proportioned build with a silky medium coat feels like a living cushion that fits easily on laps or beside a desk. This compact substance lets them adapt to family routines without needing much space.
answers.barking: Cavalier King Charles Spaniels do not bark a lot. Bred purely for companionship rather than guarding they remain quiet unless something genuinely unusual occurs. Their gentle and sociable temperament produces only occasional alert sounds rather than persistent noise, making them unobtrusive in daily life.
answers.apartment: Yes — Cavalier King Charles Spaniels can live in an apartment. Their low energy, minimal barking and adaptable nature let them settle indoors comfortably after a couple of short daily walks. The small silky-coated build and affectionate personality mean they thrive on human company without needing a large living area.
answers.first-time: Yes — Cavalier King Charles Spaniels can be a good first dog for those prepared to manage their health demands. Their high affection, gentle temperament and adaptability make daily life straightforward yet the low robustness and risk of heart conditions require consistent veterinary attention that novices must learn to provide.
